# Columns

## Basic columns

The **.a_columns** container distributes nested **.a_column** across the width. Without explicit widths, columns stretch evenly.

```html
<div class="a_columns">
  <div class="a_column">
    <div class="a_bg_gray_200 a_height_6 a_p_2 a_text_center"><span lang="en">auto</span></div>
  </div>
  <div class="a_column">
    <div class="a_bg_gray_300 a_height_6 a_p_2 a_text_center"><span lang="en">auto</span></div>
  </div>
  <div class="a_column">
    <div class="a_bg_gray_200 a_height_6 a_p_2 a_text_center"><span lang="en">auto</span></div>
  </div>
  <div class="a_column">
    <div class="a_bg_gray_300 a_height_6 a_p_2 a_text_center"><span lang="en">auto</span></div>
  </div>
</div>
```

## Grid and sizes

The **.a_columns_count_{n}** class sets the number of columns (1-12), enables wrapping, and defines the **--a_column_count** variable. Column width is set with **.a_column_{n}** and is calculated relative to the chosen count.

```html
<div class="a_columns a_columns_count_8 a_mb_4">
  <div class="a_column a_column_5">
    <div class="a_bg_gray_200 a_height_6 a_p_2 a_text_center">5/8</div>
  </div>
  <div class="a_column a_column_3">
    <div class="a_bg_gray_300 a_height_6 a_p_2 a_text_center">3/8</div>
  </div>
</div>
<div class="a_columns a_columns_count_7 a_mb_4">
  <div class="a_column a_column_2">
    <div class="a_bg_gray_300 a_height_6 a_p_2 a_text_center">2/7</div>
  </div>
  <div class="a_column a_column_2">
    <div class="a_bg_gray_200 a_height_6 a_p_2 a_text_center">2/7</div>
  </div>
  <div class="a_column a_column_3">
    <div class="a_bg_gray_300 a_height_6 a_p_2 a_text_center">3/7</div>
  </div>
</div>
<div class="a_columns a_columns_count_12 a_mb_4">
  <div class="a_column a_column_6">
    <div class="a_bg_gray_200 a_height_6 a_p_2 a_text_center">6/12</div>
  </div>
  <div class="a_column a_column_3">
    <div class="a_bg_gray_300 a_height_6 a_p_2 a_text_center">3/12</div>
  </div>
  <div class="a_column a_column_3">
    <div class="a_bg_gray_200 a_height_6 a_p_2 a_text_center">3/12</div>
  </div>
</div>
<div class="a_columns a_columns_count_12">
  <div class="a_column a_column_4">
    <div class="a_bg_gray_300 a_height_6 a_p_2 a_text_center">4/12</div>
  </div>
  <div class="a_column a_column_4">
    <div class="a_bg_gray_200 a_height_6 a_p_2 a_text_center">4/12</div>
```

## Column gaps

Gaps are set with **.a_columns_gap_x_{0-8}** and **.a_columns_gap_y_{0-8}**. By default both axes use 0.75rem.

```html
  <div class="a_column a_column_4">

  <div class="a_column a_column_4">
    <div class="a_bg_gray_300 a_height_6 a_p_2 a_text_center">4/12</div>

  <div class="a_column a_column_4">
    <div class="a_bg_gray_200 a_height_6 a_p_2 a_text_center">4/12</div>
  </div>
</div>
<p class="a_mb_2"><code class="a_color_danger">.a_columns_gap_x_6</code> <code class="a_color_danger">.a_columns_gap_y_6</code></p>

  <div class="a_column a_column_4">

  <div class="a_column a_column_4">
```

## Offsets

Left offset: **.a_column_offset_{n}**, right offset: **.a_column_offset_right_{n}**, where **n** is 0 to 11.

```html
<p class="a_mb_2"><code class="a_color_danger">.a_column_offset_2</code></p>
<div class="a_columns a_columns_count_12 a_mb_4">
  <div class="a_column a_column_4 a_column_offset_2">
    <div class="a_bg_gray_200 a_height_6 a_p_2 a_text_center">4/12 + <span lang="en">offset</span> 2</div>
  </div>
  <div class="a_column a_column_4">
    <div class="a_bg_gray_300 a_height_6 a_p_2 a_text_center">4/12</div>
  </div>
</div>
<p class="a_mb_2"><code class="a_color_danger">.a_column_offset_right_2</code></p>
<div class="a_columns a_columns_count_12">
  <div class="a_column a_column_4">
    <div class="a_bg_gray_200 a_height_6 a_p_2 a_text_center">4/12</div>
  </div>
  <div class="a_column a_column_4 a_column_offset_right_2">
    <div class="a_bg_gray_300 a_height_6 a_p_2 a_text_center">4/12 + <span lang="en">offset</span> <span lang="en">right</span> 2</div>
  </div>
</div>
```

## Responsive classes

Add the suffixes **_mobile**, **_tablet**, **_touch**, **_desktop**, **_widescreen**, **_fullhd**, **_large** to **.a_columns_count_***, **.a_columns_gap_***, **.a_column_***, **.a_column_offset_***. Breakpoints: mobile <= 768px, tablet 769-1023px, touch <= 1023px, desktop 1024-1215px, widescreen 1216-1407px, fullhd 1408-1599px, large >= 1600px.

```html
<p class="a_mb_2">
  <code class="a_color_danger">.a_column_12_mobile</code>
  <code class="a_color_danger">.a_column_6_tablet</code>
  <code class="a_color_danger">.a_column_4_desktop</code>
</p>
<div class="a_columns a_columns_count_12">
  <div class="a_column a_column_12_mobile a_column_6_tablet a_column_4_desktop">
    <div class="a_bg_gray_200 a_height_6 a_p_2 a_text_center"><span lang="en">mobile</span> 12 / <span lang="en">tablet</span> 6 / <span lang="en">desktop</span> 4</div>
  </div>
  <div class="a_column a_column_12_mobile a_column_6_tablet a_column_4_desktop">
    <div class="a_bg_gray_300 a_height_6 a_p_2 a_text_center"><span lang="en">mobile</span> 12 / <span lang="en">tablet</span> 6 / <span lang="en">desktop</span> 4</div>
  </div>
  <div class="a_column a_column_12_mobile a_column_6_tablet a_column_4_desktop">
    <div class="a_bg_gray_200 a_height_6 a_p_2 a_text_center"><span lang="en">mobile</span> 12 / <span lang="en">tablet</span> 6 / <span lang="en">desktop</span> 4</div>
  </div>
</div>
```

# Text Styles

```html
<div class="a_fs_1"><code class="a_color_danger">.a_fs_1</code> Text</div>
<div class="a_fs_2"><code class="a_color_danger">.a_fs_2</code> Text</div>
<div class="a_fs_3"><code class="a_color_danger">.a_fs_3</code> Text</div>
<div class="a_fs_4"><code class="a_color_danger">.a_fs_4</code> Text</div>
<div class="a_fs_5"><code class="a_color_danger">.a_fs_5</code> Text</div>
<div class="a_fs_6"><code class="a_color_danger">.a_fs_6</code> Text</div>
<div class="a_fs_7"><code class="a_color_danger">.a_fs_7</code> Text</div>
```

```html
<div class="a_text_left_fullhd"><code class="a_color_danger">.a_text_left_fullhd</code> Text</div>
<div class="a_text_right_fullhd"><code class="a_color_danger">.a_text_right_fullhd</code> Text</div>
<div class="a_text_center_fullhd"><code class="a_color_danger">.a_text_center_fullhd</code> Text</div>
<div class="a_text_justify_fullhd"><code class="a_color_danger">.a_text_justify_fullhd</code> Text</div>
<br>
<div class="a_text_left_large"><code class="a_color_danger">.a_text_left_large</code> Text</div>
<div class="a_text_right_large"><code class="a_color_danger">.a_text_right_large</code> Text</div>
<div class="a_text_center_large"><code class="a_color_danger">.a_text_center_large</code> Text</div>
<div class="a_text_justify_large"><code class="a_color_danger">.a_text_justify_large</code> Text</div>
```

## Text Transformation

**CSS** classes for changing text case and formatting. Use **.a_text_lowercase** for lowercase, **.a_text_uppercase** for uppercase, **.a_text_capitalize** for capitalizing the first letter of each word, as well as classes for underlining and striking through text. **.a_text_underline_offset** underlines the text with a little space under it, **.a_text_line_through_muted** strikes through secondary text, e.g. an old price.

```html
<div><code class="a_color_danger a_mr_2">.a_text_lowercase</code><span class="a_text_lowercase">TEXT</span></div>
<div><code class="a_color_danger a_mr_2">.a_text_uppercase</code><span class="a_text_uppercase">Text</span></div>
<div><code class="a_color_danger a_mr_2">.a_text_capitalize</code><span class="a_text_capitalize">text</span></div>
<div><code class="a_color_danger a_mr_2">.a_text_underline</code><span class="a_text_underline">Text</span></div>
<div><code class="a_color_danger a_mr_2">.a_text_line_through</code><span class="a_text_line_through">Text</span></div>
<div><code class="a_color_danger a_mr_2">.a_text_decoration_none</code><span class="a_text_decoration_none">Text</span></div>
<div><code class="a_color_danger a_mr_2">.a_text_underline_offset</code><span class="a_text_underline_offset">Text</span></div>
<div><code class="a_color_danger a_mr_2">.a_text_line_through_muted</code><span class="a_text_line_through_muted">49,99 €</span><strong class="a_ml_2">39,99 €</strong></div>
```

## Font Weight

**CSS** classes for controlling font weight and style. Includes options from light (**.a_text_light**) to bold (**.a_text_bold**, **.a_text_bolder**), as well as italic (**.a_text_italic**) and normal style (**.a_text_normal**).

```html
<div class="a_text_bold"><code class="a_color_danger a_mr_2">.a_text_bold</code>Text</div>
<div class="a_text_bolder"><code class="a_color_danger a_mr_2">.a_text_bolder</code>Text</div>
<div class="a_text_semibold"><code class="a_color_danger a_mr_2">.a_text_semibold</code>Text</div>
<div class="a_text_light"><code class="a_color_danger a_mr_2">.a_text_light</code>Text</div>
<div class="a_text_lighter"><code class="a_color_danger a_mr_2">.a_text_lighter</code>Text</div>
<div class="a_text_italic"><code class="a_color_danger a_mr_2">.a_text_italic</code>Text</div>
<div class="a_text_normal"><code class="a_color_danger a_mr_2">.a_text_normal</code>Text</div>
```

## Monospace and numbers

**.a_text_monospace** sets the monospace font for IDs, hashes and code. **.a_text_tabular_nums** gives all digits the same width, so numbers in columns line up.

```html
<span class="a_text_monospace">3f9a1c7e-42b0-4d1e</span>

<div class="a_text_tabular_nums a_text_right">
  <div>1 111,11</div>
  <div>8 888,88</div>
  <div>10 101,01</div>
</div>
```

## Text Wrapping

**CSS** classes for controlling text wrapping. Includes normal wrapping (**.a_text_wrap**), no wrapping (**.a_text_nowrap**), forced wrapping of long words (**.a_text_break**), hyphenated wrapping (**.a_text_wrap_hyphens**), and truncation with ellipsis (**.a_text_truncate**).

```html
<div><code class="a_color_danger a_mr_2">.a_text_wrap</code><div class="a_badge a_text_wrap" style="width: 6rem;">Lorem ipsum dolor sit amet consectetur adipisicing elit</div></div>
<div class="a_mt_3"><code class="a_color_danger a_mr_2">.a_text_nowrap</code><div class="a_text_nowrap a_bg_gray_300" style="width: 6rem;">Lorem ipsum dolor sit amet consectetur adipisicing elit</div></div>
<div class="a_mt_3"><code class="a_color_danger a_mr_2">.a_text_break</code><div class="a_text_break" style="width: 10rem;">aaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaa</div></div>
<div class="a_mt_3"><code class="a_color_danger a_mr_2">.a_text_wrap_hyphens</code><div class="a_text_wrap_hyphens" lang="en" style="width: 10rem;">pneumonoultramicroscopicsilicovolcanoconiosis</div></div>
<div class="a_mt_3"><code class="a_color_danger a_mr_2">.a_text_truncate</code><div class="a_text_truncate" style="width: 6rem;">Lorem ipsum dolor sit amet consectetur adipisicing elit</div></div>
```

## Text Line Limiting

**CSS** classes for limiting the number of displayed text lines with an ellipsis at the end. The base class **.a_text_clamp** limits text to one line, while modifiers **.a_text_clamp_2** - **.a_text_clamp_5** allow displaying the corresponding number of lines.

```html
<div>
  <code class="a_color_danger a_mr_2">.a_text_clamp</code>
```

<!-- https://ilia-brykin.github.io/aloha/llms/css/tile.md -->

# Tile

The class `a_tile` is a box on the surface with a border and rounded corners, e.g. for a summary, a dashboard widget or an item in a list of results. It is CSS only, the parts `a_tile__header`, `a_tile__body`, `a_tile__footer` are optional.

## Basic

`a_tile` with `a_tile__body`. The tile is a flex column, so `a_tile__body` fills the free height.

```html
<div class="a_tile">
  <div class="a_tile__body">
    A tile groups related content on the surface.
  </div>
</div>
```

## Header and footer

`a_tile__header` and `a_tile__footer` get a subtle background and a line to the body. Use a heading of the right level (`h2` … `h6`) in the header, so the structure of the page stays correct for screen readers.

```html
<div class="a_tile">
  <div class="a_tile__header">
    <h3 class="a_fs_5">Invoice 2026-114</h3>
  </div>
  <div class="a_tile__body">
    <p>Amount: 1.234,50 €</p>
    <p>Due on 01.12.2026</p>
  </div>
  <div class="a_tile__footer a_d_flex a_gap_2">
    <button class="a_btn a_btn_primary" type="button">Pay</button>
    <button class="a_btn a_btn_secondary" type="button">Details</button>
  </div>
</div>
```

## Clickable tile

With `a_stretched_link` on the link the whole tile is clickable, `a_bg_{color}_subtle_hover` highlights it on hover. Keyboard and screen reader users still get one link with a clear text. Other buttons in the tile need `a_position_relative` and `a_z_index_2`.

```html
<div class="a_tile a_bg_primary_subtle_hover">
  <div class="a_tile__body">
    <h3 class="a_fs_5">
      <a class="a_stretched_link" href="/projects/1">Project Aloha</a>
    </h3>
    <p>The whole tile is clickable.</p>
  </div>
</div>
```

## Colors, shadow and border

The tile is changed with the utility classes: border color (`a_border_{color}`, `a_border_{color}_subtle`), shadow (`a_shadow_sm` / `_md` / `_lg`), line style (`a_border_style_dashed`). The defaults and the corner radius are set with the CSS variables below.

```html
<div class="a_tile a_border_primary_subtle">...</div>
<div class="a_tile a_border_danger">...</div>
<div class="a_tile a_shadow_md a_border_0">...</div>
<div class="a_tile a_border_style_dashed">...</div>
```

## Tiles in a grid

Tiles in `a_columns`. With `a_height_100` all tiles of a row get the same height, `a_columns_count_1_mobile` shows one tile per row on mobile devices.

```html
<div class="a_columns a_columns_count_3 a_columns_count_1_mobile">
  <div class="a_column a_column_1">
    <div class="a_tile a_height_100">...</div>
  </div>
  <div class="a_column a_column_1">
    <div class="a_tile a_height_100">...</div>
  </div>
  <div class="a_column a_column_1">
    <div class="a_tile a_height_100">...</div>
  </div>
</div>
```

## CSS variables (`scss/utils/tile.scss`)

| name | value | description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `--a_tile_padding_x` |  | Horizontal padding of all parts. |
| `--a_tile_padding_y` |  | Vertical padding of the body. |
| `--a_tile_header_padding_y` |  | Vertical padding of the header and the footer. |
| `--a_tile_color` |  | Text color. |
| `--a_tile_bg` |  | Background. |
| `--a_tile_border_width` |  | Width of the border and of the lines below the header and above the footer. |
| `--a_tile_border_color` |  | Border color. The classes .a_border_{color} and .a_border_{color}_subtle also work. |
| `--a_tile_border_radius` |  | Corner radius. |
| `--a_tile_shadow` |  | Shadow. The classes .a_shadow_sm / _md / _lg also work. |
| `--a_tile_header_bg` |  | Background of the header and the footer. |
| `--a_tile_header_font_weight` |  | Font weight of the header. |

<!-- https://ilia-brykin.github.io/aloha/llms/css/utilities.md -->

# Utilities

## Focus ring

The two-colored focus ring of the components for own focusable elements, e.g. a card with `tabindex="0"`. It is shown for keyboard focus only and is configured with the focus tokens.

```html
<div class="a_focus_ring a_p_3 a_border" tabindex="0">
  a_focus_ring
</div>
<div class="a_focus_ring_inset a_p_3 a_border" tabindex="0">
  a_focus_ring_inset
</div>
```

## Text color

Secondary and emphasized text that stays readable in the light and the dark theme.

```html
<p class="a_text_muted">a_text_muted</p>
<p class="a_text_emphasis">a_text_emphasis</p>
```

## Stack

`a_vstack` places the items one below the other (flex column), `a_hstack` next to each other and centers them vertically (flex row). The space between the items is set with `a_gap_*`, `a_ml_auto` pushes an item to the end.

```html
<div class="a_vstack a_gap_2">
  <div>1</div>
  <div>2</div>
  <div>3</div>
</div>

<div class="a_hstack a_gap_2">
  <div>1</div>
  <div>2</div>
  <div class="a_ml_auto">a_ml_auto</div>
</div>
```

## Sizing

Classes set the width and the height: `a_width_*` / `a_height_*` (`1` … `6`, `25` … `100` %, `1rem` … `3rem`, `auto`; `a_width_50px` … `a_width_400px`), `a_max_width_*` (`300px` … `800px`, `25` … `100` %, `none`), `a_max_height_100`, `a_max_height_none`, `a_min_width_0`, `a_min_width_100`, `a_min_height_0`, `a_min_height_100`. `a_min_width_0` lets a flex item shrink below the width of its content, e.g. for `a_text_truncate`. `a_viewport_height_100` and `a_min_viewport_height_100` use `100vh`, the variants `_100dvh` use the visible height on mobile devices with browser bars. Suffixes `_mobile` … `_large` enable them at breakpoints.

```html
<div class="a_width_25">a_width_25</div>
<div class="a_width_50">a_width_50</div>
<div class="a_max_width_400px">a_max_width_400px</div>

<!-- a_min_width_0: the flex item can shrink, the text is truncated -->
<div class="a_hstack a_gap_2">
  <div class="a_flex_shrink_0">Label</div>
  <div class="a_min_width_0 a_text_truncate">A long text ...</div>
</div>

<!-- full height of the visible area, also on mobile with browser bars -->
<div class="a_min_viewport_height_100dvh">...</div>

<!-- only on mobile -->
<div class="a_width_100_mobile">...</div>
```

## Aspect ratio

Classes set the `aspect-ratio` of an element: `a_ratio_1x1`, `a_ratio_4x3`, `a_ratio_16x9`, `a_ratio_21x9`. The height follows the width, e.g. for videos, maps and image placeholders.

```html
<div class="a_ratio_1x1">a_ratio_1x1</div>
<div class="a_ratio_4x3">a_ratio_4x3</div>
<div class="a_ratio_16x9">a_ratio_16x9</div>
<div class="a_ratio_21x9">a_ratio_21x9</div>

<iframe class="a_ratio_16x9 a_width_100" src="..." title="Video"></iframe>
```

## Object fit

Classes set how an image or a video fills its box (`object-fit`): `a_object_fit_cover` fills the box and crops the image, `a_object_fit_contain` shows the whole image, `a_object_fit_fill` stretches it, `a_object_fit_none` keeps the original size, `a_object_fit_scale_down` uses `none` or `contain`, whichever is smaller.

```html
<img class="a_object_fit_cover" src="image.png" alt="" style="width: 10rem; height: 6rem;">
<img class="a_object_fit_contain" src="image.png" alt="" style="width: 10rem; height: 6rem;">
<img class="a_object_fit_fill" src="image.png" alt="" style="width: 10rem; height: 6rem;">
<img class="a_object_fit_none" src="image.png" alt="" style="width: 10rem; height: 6rem;">
<img class="a_object_fit_scale_down" src="image.png" alt="" style="width: 10rem; height: 6rem;">
```

## Stretched link

`a_stretched_link` makes the whole parent with `a_position_relative` clickable, e.g. a card. There is still only one link with a clear text for keyboard and screen reader users. Other links and buttons in the card need `a_position_relative` and `a_z_index_2` to stay clickable.

```html
<div class="a_position_relative a_border a_p_3 a_bg_primary_subtle_hover">
  <p>The whole card is clickable.</p>
  <a class="a_stretched_link" href="/details">a_stretched_link</a>
</div>
```

## Hover

Colors on hover and keyboard focus. `a_link_muted` is a link in the muted text color that gets the link color on hover. `a_bg_{color}_hover` sets the hover tone of a color, e.g. together with `a_bg_primary`. `a_bg_{color}_subtle_hover` sets the subtle background, e.g. for list items and cards. Colors: `primary`, `secondary`, `tertiary`, `success`, `info`, `warning`, `danger`, `light`, `dark`.

```html
<a class="a_link_muted" href="#">a_link_muted</a>

<button class="a_btn a_bg_primary a_bg_primary_hover a_color_white" type="button">
  a_bg_primary_hover
</button>

<div class="a_bg_primary_subtle_hover" tabindex="0">a_bg_primary_subtle_hover</div>
```

## Corner radius

Classes set the corner radius from the `--a_border_radius_*` tokens: `a_radius_small`, `a_radius`, `a_radius_large`, `a_radius_xl`, `a_radius_2xl`. `a_pill_rounded` makes the corners fully round, `a_rounded_circle` makes a square element a circle, `a_rounded_0` removes the radius.

```html
<div class="a_radius_small a_border a_p_3">a_radius_small</div>
<div class="a_radius a_border a_p_3">a_radius</div>
<div class="a_radius_large a_border a_p_3">a_radius_large</div>
<div class="a_radius_xl a_border a_p_3">a_radius_xl</div>
<div class="a_radius_2xl a_border a_p_3">a_radius_2xl</div>
<div class="a_pill_rounded a_border a_p_3">a_pill_rounded</div>
```

## Border style and color

`a_border_style_dashed` and `a_border_style_dotted` change the line of `a_border`, `a_border_top`, `a_border_right`, `a_border_bottom`, `a_border_left`, `a_tile`. `a_border_{color}_subtle` sets a light border color that fits the `a_bg_{color}_subtle` backgrounds. Colors: `primary`, `secondary`, `tertiary`, `success`, `info`, `warning`, `danger`, `light`, `dark`.

```html
<div class="a_border a_border_style_dashed">a_border_style_dashed</div>
<div class="a_border a_border_style_dotted">a_border_style_dotted</div>

<!-- also with one side or a color -->
<div class="a_border_top a_border_style_dashed a_border_primary">...</div>

<div class="a_border a_border_primary_subtle">a_border_primary_subtle</div>
<div class="a_border a_border_success_subtle">a_border_success_subtle</div>
<div class="a_border a_border_warning_subtle">a_border_warning_subtle</div>
<div class="a_border a_border_danger_subtle">a_border_danger_subtle</div>
```

## Vertical divider

`a_divider_vertical` draws a vertical line between the items of a row, e.g. in `a_hstack`. It takes the height of the row and the color of `a_divider` (`--a_divider_bg`). A decorative line gets `aria-hidden="true"`; a line that separates groups of controls gets `role="separator"` + `aria-orientation="vertical"`.

```html
<div class="a_hstack a_gap_3">
  <span>Text</span>
  <span class="a_divider_vertical" aria-hidden="true"></span>
  <span>Text</span>
  <span class="a_divider_vertical" aria-hidden="true"></span>
  <button class="a_btn a_btn_primary" type="button">Button</button>
</div>
```

## Shadow

Classes set the shadow from the `--a_shadow_*` tokens: `a_shadow_sm`, `a_shadow_md`, `a_shadow_lg`. `a_shadow_none` removes a shadow. The shadows are adapted for the dark theme.

```html
<div class="a_shadow_none a_p_3">a_shadow_none</div>
<div class="a_shadow_sm a_p_3">a_shadow_sm</div>
<div class="a_shadow_md a_p_3">a_shadow_md</div>
<div class="a_shadow_lg a_p_3">a_shadow_lg</div>
```

## Circle

`a_rounded_circle` makes a square element round, e.g. an avatar or a status dot.

```html
<img class="a_rounded_circle" src="avatar.png" alt="" width="48" height="48">
<span class="a_rounded_circle a_bg_success a_d_inline_block" style="width: .75rem; height: .75rem;"></span>
```

## Visibility

`a_invisible` hides an element, but it keeps its place in the layout, unlike `a_d_none`. `a_visible` shows it again. A hidden element is also hidden for screen readers.

```html
<!-- the element is hidden, but keeps its place -->
<div class="a_invisible">...</div>

<!-- the element is hidden and takes no place -->
<div class="a_d_none">...</div>
```

## Cursor

Classes set the mouse `cursor`: `a_cursor_pointer`, `a_cursor_default`, `a_cursor_not_allowed`, `a_cursor_move`, `a_cursor_text`, `a_cursor_help`, `a_cursor_grab`, `a_cursor_grabbing`, `a_cursor_wait`, `a_cursor_crosshair`. Hover over the elements.

```html
<div class="a_cursor_pointer">a_cursor_pointer</div>
<div class="a_cursor_default">a_cursor_default</div>
<div class="a_cursor_not_allowed">a_cursor_not_allowed</div>
<div class="a_cursor_move">a_cursor_move</div>
<div class="a_cursor_text">a_cursor_text</div>
<div class="a_cursor_help">a_cursor_help</div>
<div class="a_cursor_grab">a_cursor_grab</div>
<div class="a_cursor_grabbing">a_cursor_grabbing</div>
<div class="a_cursor_wait">a_cursor_wait</div>
<div class="a_cursor_crosshair">a_cursor_crosshair</div>
```

## Pointer events

`a_pointer_events_none` makes an element ignore the mouse and touch, `a_pointer_events_auto` turns them on again for a child element. The keyboard still works, so also set `tabindex="-1"` and `aria-disabled` for a disabled link.

```html
<a class="a_pointer_events_none" href="#" tabindex="-1" aria-disabled="true">a_pointer_events_none</a>

<div class="a_pointer_events_none">
  <a class="a_pointer_events_auto" href="#">a_pointer_events_auto</a>
</div>
```

## Text selection

With `a_text_select_all` one click selects the whole text, e.g. an ID or a token to copy. `a_text_select_none` prevents selecting the text.

```html
<span class="a_text_select_all a_text_monospace">3f9a1c7e-42b0-4d1e-9c55</span>
<span class="a_text_select_none">Text</span>
```

## Opacity

Classes set `opacity` to 0, 25, 50, 75 or 100 %.

```html
<div class="a_opacity_100 a_bg_primary a_p_2">a_opacity_100</div>
<div class="a_opacity_75 a_bg_primary a_p_2">a_opacity_75</div>
<div class="a_opacity_50 a_bg_primary a_p_2">a_opacity_50</div>
<div class="a_opacity_25 a_bg_primary a_p_2">a_opacity_25</div>
<div class="a_opacity_0 a_bg_primary a_p_2">a_opacity_0</div>
```

## Order

Classes set the `order` of flex and grid items: `a_order_first` (−1), `a_order_0` … `a_order_5`, `a_order_last` (6). Suffixes `_mobile` … `_large` enable them at breakpoints.

```html
<div class="a_d_flex a_gap_2">
  <div class="a_order_last">1: a_order_last</div>
  <div class="a_order_2">2: a_order_2</div>
  <div class="a_order_first">3: a_order_first</div>
  <div class="a_order_1">4: a_order_1</div>
</div>

<!-- only on mobile: the last element is shown first -->
<div class="a_order_first_mobile">...</div>
```

## Z-index

Global layers use the `--a_z_index_*` tokens, so own overlays stay in the right order with modals, dropdowns and popups.

```html
<div class="a_position_fixed a_z_index_popup">...</div>

<!-- local stacking inside a component -->
<div class="a_position_relative a_z_index_1">...</div>
```

## Print

`a_print_none` hides an element when printing, `a_print_block` shows it only in print (together with `a_d_none`).

```html
<nav class="a_print_none">...</nav>
<div class="a_d_none a_print_block">Printed on ...</div>
```

<!-- https://ilia-brykin.github.io/aloha/llms/directives/on-hooks.md -->

# AOnHooks (Function calls at different lifecycle stages)

AOnHooks is a powerful Vue.js directive allowing for binding of the specific functions executions when different lifecycle stages of a Vue.js component or HTML tag are reached. This directive provides an elegant way to run code at the different stages of the component or tag lifecycle, allowing granular control over the behavior of a Vue.js component or HTML element.

The directive exports a collection of hooks that can be bound to the specific lifecycle methods of a Vue.js component or HTML tag. These hooks allow code to be executed at the following moments:

- **created:** This function is called before any attributes or event listeners are applied to the bound element. This hook provides a great opportunity to run initializing code and make preparations before the element appears in the DOM.
- **beforeMount:** The function that is bound here is called just before the element is inserted into the DOM. This hook is useful for making final changes to the DOM before the element becomes visible.
- **mounted:** Once the element or component is fully mounted in the DOM, the function bound here is called. This hook provides a convenient place to make asynchronous requests or access external resources after the element has been fully rendered.
- **beforeUnmount:** Before the element or component is unmounted, the function bound here is called. Cleanup code can be placed here, for example to remove event listeners or release the resources.
- **unmounted:** This function is called when the element or component is unmounted. It's the last chance to do any cleanup and any resource releases.

## Basic usage

```html
<div
  v-a-on-hooks="{ created: onCreated, beforeMount: onBeforeMount, mounted: onMounted, beforeUnmount: onBeforeUnmount, unmounted: onUnmounted }"
>Lorem ipsum dolor sit amet, consectetur adipiscing elit.</div>
```

```js
import {
  AOnHooks,
} from "aloha-vue";
    
export default {
  name: "PageOnHooksExample",
  directives: {
    AOnHooks,
  },
  setup() {
    const onCreated = (el, binding) => {
      console.log("created", el, binding);
    };
    
    const onBeforeMount = (el, binding) => {
      console.log("beforeMount", el, binding);
    };
    
    const onMounted = (el, binding) => {
      console.log("mounted", el, binding);
    };
    
    const onBeforeUnmount = (el, binding) => {
      console.log("beforeUnmount", el, binding);
    }; 
    
    const onUnmounted = (el, binding) => {
      console.log("unmounted", el, binding);
    };

    return {
      onBeforeMount,
      onBeforeUnmount,
      onCreated,
      onMounted,
      onUnmounted,
    };
  },
};
```

# filterBoolean

The function **filterBoolean** is used to convert a **boolean value** into translated text. It allows customization of the texts for **True** and **False** values and the option to return an empty string for **undefined** or **null**.

## Import as Function

```js
import { filterBoolean } from "aloha-vue";
```

## Import as composition API

```js
import { AFiltersAPI } from "aloha-vue";

export default {
  setup() {  
    const {
      filterBoolean,
    } = AFiltersAPI();
  },
};
```

## Arguments

```js
filterBoolean(value, { [trueValue="_YES_"], [falseValue="_NO_"], [useNil=true] })
```

- **value** (Any): The value to be converted into translated text
- **[trueValue="_YES_"]** (String): The translated text to be returned in case the value is **True**
- **[falseValue="_NO_"]** (String): The translated text to be returned in case the value is **False**
- **[useNil=true]** (Boolean): Indicates whether an empty string should be returned for **undefined** or **null**

## Basic usage

```js
filterBoolean(true);
// Yes
filterBoolean(false);
// No

filterBoolean(1);
// Yes
filterBoolean(0);
// No

filterBoolean("aloha");
// Yes
filterBoolean("");
// No
```

## trueValue, falseValue

```js
filterBoolean(true, { trueValue: "1", falseValue: "0" });
// 1
filterBoolean(false, { trueValue: "1", falseValue: "0" });
// 0

filterBoolean(1, { trueValue: "true", falseValue: "false" });
// true
filterBoolean(0, { trueValue: "true", falseValue: "false" });
// false
```

## useNil

```js
filterBoolean(null, { useNil: true });
// 
filterBoolean(null, { useNil: false });
// No

filterBoolean(undefined, { useNil: true });
// 
filterBoolean(undefined, { useNil: false });
// No

filterBoolean("null", { useNil: true });
// Yes
filterBoolean("null", { useNil: false });
// Yes

filterBoolean("undefined", { useNil: true });
// Yes
filterBoolean("undefined", { useNil: false });
// Yes
```

# filterCurrency

The function **filterCurrency** is a specialized extension of the [**filterFloat**](https://ilia-brykin.github.io/aloha/llms/functions/filter-float.md) function and serves to format numeric values as currency. It accepts a numeric value and returns a string that represents the value with the specified currency, number of decimal places, a suffix, and optional digit grouping (thousands separator). If the numeric value is not specified (null or undefined), an empty string is returned. This function is designed to be extended for many currencies.

## Import as Function

```js
import { filterCurrency } from "aloha-vue";
```

## Import as composition API

```js
import { AFiltersAPI } from "aloha-vue";

export default {
  setup() {  
    const {
      filterCurrency,
    } = AFiltersAPI();
  },
};
```

## Arguments

```js
filterCurrency(value, { [suffix="€"], [digits=2], [digitGrouping=true] })
```

- **value** (Number | String): The numeric value to be formatted as currency
- **[suffix="€"]** (String): The suffix added to the formatted string to denote the currency
- **[digits=2]** (Number): The number of decimal places in the formatted string
- **[digitGrouping=true]** (Boolean): Indicates whether digit grouping is enabled to insert thousands separators in the formatted string

## Basic usage

```js
filterCurrency(123456);
// 123.456,00 €

filterCurrency("1000000.2345");
// 1.000.000,23 €

filterCurrency("aloha");
// aloha

filterCurrency(undefined);
//
```

## suffix

```js
filterCurrency(2000, { suffix: "€" });
// 2.000,00 €

filterCurrency("25.5", { suffix: "%" });
// 25,50 %
```

## digits

```js
filterCurrency(2000, { digits: 0 });
// 2.000 €

filterCurrency("25.53451", { digits: 4 });
// 25,5345 €
```

## digitGrouping

```js
filterCurrency(1000222.55, { digitGrouping: false });
// 1000222,55 €

filterCurrency(1000222.55, { digitGrouping: true });
// 1.000.222,55 €
```

# filterDate

The function **filterDate** uses the [moment.js](https://momentjs.com/docs/#/displaying/format/) library to format dates and times. It takes a date or time value and returns it in the specified format. Note that moment.js is considered a deprecated library and is planned to be replaced by another solution in the future. There are also plans to expand the function to support various languages.

## Import as Function

```js
import { filterDate } from "aloha-vue";
```

## Import as composition API

```js
import { AFiltersAPI } from "aloha-vue";

export default {
  setup() {  
    const {
      filterDate,
    } = AFiltersAPI();
  },
};
```

## Arguments

```js
filterDate(value, { [format="date"] })
```

- **value** (Any): The date or time to be formatted
- **[format="date"]** (String): The display format for the date. Possible values: "date" (date), "datetime" (date and time), "fullDate" (full date and time), "time" (time), "timeWithSeconds" (time with seconds) or a valid format from [moment.js](https://momentjs.com/docs/#/displaying/format/)

## Basic usage

```js
filterDate("2014-09-08T08:02:17-05:00");
// 08.09.2014

filterDate("2013-02-08");
// 08.02.2013

filterDate("6 Mar 17 21:22 UT");
// 06.03.2017
```

## format

```js
filterDate("2014-09-08T08:02:17-05:00" { format: "datetime" });
// 08.09.2014 15:02

filterDate("2014-09-08T08:02:17-05:00", { format: "fullDate" });
// Monday, 08. September 2014, 15:02

filterDate("2014-09-08T08:02:17-05:00", { format: "time" });
// 15:02

filterDate("2014-09-08T08:02:17-05:00", { format: "timeWithSeconds" });
// 15:02:17

filterDate("2014-09-08T08:02:17-05:00", { format: "MM.YYYY" });
// 09.2014
```

# filterDateRelative

The function **filterDateRelative** formats a date relative to now, e.g. "5 minutes ago" or "in 2 days". The text is in the current language (`Intl.RelativeTimeFormat`). Use **filterDate** for an absolute date.

## Import as Function

```js
import { filterDateRelative } from "aloha-vue";
```

## Import as composition API

```js
import { AFiltersAPI } from "aloha-vue";

export default {
  setup() {  
    const {
      filterDateRelative,
    } = AFiltersAPI();
  },
};
```

## Arguments

```js
filterDateRelative(value, { [now=new Date()], [numeric="auto"] })
```

- **value** (String | Date): The date
- **[now=new Date()]** (String | Date): The date the value is compared to
- **[numeric="auto"]** (String): "auto" ("yesterday", "tomorrow") or "always" ("1 day ago", "in 1 day")

## Basic usage

```js
filterDateRelative(new Date(Date.now() - 5 * 60 * 1000));
// 5 minutes ago

filterDateRelative(new Date(Date.now() + 2 * 24 * 60 * 60 * 1000));
// tomorrow

filterDateRelative("Aloha");
// Aloha
```

## numeric

```js
filterDateRelative("2026-03-09T12:00:00", { now: "2026-03-10T12:00:00" });
// yesterday

filterDateRelative("2026-03-09T12:00:00", { now: "2026-03-10T12:00:00", numeric: "always" });
// 1 day ago
```

## now

```js
filterDateRelative("2026-01-01", { now: "2026-03-10" });
// 2 months ago

filterDateRelative("2026-03-10T12:00:00", { now: "2026-03-10T11:58:00" });
// in 2 minutes
```

# filterDuration

The function **filterDuration** formats a duration, e.g. of a process or a video: as text with units (**1 h 2 min 5 s**) or as a clock (**01:02:05**). The value is rounded to whole seconds.

## Import as Function

```js
import { filterDuration } from "aloha-vue";
```

## Import as composition API

```js
import { AFiltersAPI } from "aloha-vue";

export default {
  setup() {  
    const {
      filterDuration,
    } = AFiltersAPI();
  },
};
```

## Arguments

```js
filterDuration(value, { [sourceUnits="s"], [format="long"], [maxUnits=0], [showDays=true] })
```

- **value** (Number | String): The duration
- **[sourceUnits="s"]** (String): The units of the value: **ms**, **s**, **m**, **h** or **d**
- **[format="long"]** (String): **long** (text with units) or **clock** (hours:minutes:seconds)
- **[maxUnits=0]** (Number): Only for **long**: the maximum number of shown units, starting with the largest one. **0** shows all units
- **[showDays=true]** (Boolean): Only for **long**: whether days are shown. Otherwise they are counted as hours

## Basic usage

```js
filterDuration(3725);
// 1 h 2 min 5 s

filterDuration(90061);
// 1 d 1 h 1 min 1 s

filterDuration(0);
// 0 s
```

## sourceUnits

```js
filterDuration(1500, { sourceUnits: "ms" });
// 2 s

filterDuration(90, { sourceUnits: "m" });
// 1 h 30 min

filterDuration(1.5, { sourceUnits: "h" });
// 1 h 30 min
```

## format

```js
filterDuration(3725, { format: "clock" });
// 01:02:05

filterDuration(90061, { format: "clock" });
// 25:01:01
```

## maxUnits

```js
filterDuration(90061, { maxUnits: 2 });
// 1 d 1 h

filterDuration(3725, { maxUnits: 1 });
// 1 h
```

## showDays

```js
filterDuration(90061, { showDays: false });
// 25 h 1 min 1 s
```

## Translations

| key | en |
| --- | --- |
| `_A_DURATION_DAYS_` | d |
| `_A_DURATION_HOURS_` | h |
| `_A_DURATION_MINUTES_` | min |
| `_A_DURATION_SECONDS_` | s |

# filterEmail

The function **filterEmail** creates an HTML link for an email address. It checks if the email address exists and is not empty. If the conditions are met, an HTML link in the format **<a href="mailto:email" class="linkClass">email</a>** is returned.

```js
import { filterEmail } from "aloha-vue";
```

## Import as composition API

```js
import { AFiltersAPI } from "aloha-vue";

export default {
  setup() {  
    const {
      filterEmail,
    } = AFiltersAPI();
  },
};
```

## Arguments

```js
filterEmail(email, { [linkClass] })
```

- **email** (String): The email address for which the HTML link is to be created
- **[linkClass]** (String): A CSS class that will be added to the created HTML link

## Basic usage

```js
// <a href="mailto:example@example.com">example@example.com</a>
```

```js
import { AFiltersAPI } from "aloha-vue";
```

- **value** (String): The string containing potentially unsafe HTML

# filterFileSize

The function **filterFileSize** converts a size from a source unit (e.g., Bytes) to a target size in a specific unit (e.g., Kilobytes, Megabytes) and returns the result as a formatted string.

## Import as Function

```js
import { filterFileSize } from "aloha-vue";
```

## Import as composition API

```js
import { AFiltersAPI } from "aloha-vue";

export default {
  setup() {  
    const {
      filterFileSize,
    } = AFiltersAPI();
  },
};
```

## Arguments

```js
filterFileSize(value, { [units="kb"], [sourceUnits="b"], [digits=2] })
```

- **value** (Number): The size to be converted
- **[units="kb"]** (String): The desired unit for the size specification. Possible units are **b** (Bytes), **kb** (Kilobytes), **mb** (Megabytes), **gb** (Gigabytes), **tb** (Terabytes), **pb** (Petabytes), **eb** (Exabytes), **zb** (Zettabytes), **yb** (Yottabytes)
- **[sourceUnits="b"]** (String): The unit of the original size. Possible units are the same as for **units**
- **[digits=2]** (Number): The number of decimal places in the formatted string

## Basic usage

```js
filterFileSize(2000);
// 1,95 KB

filterFileSize(1024);
// 1,00 KB
```

## units

```js
filterFileSize(1024, { units: "b" });
// 1.024,00 Bytes

filterFileSize(1024, { units: "kb" });
// 1,00 KB

filterFileSize(1048576, { units: "mb" });
// 1,00 MB

filterFileSize(1073741824, { units: "gb" });
// 1,00 GB

filterFileSize(1073741824 * 1024, { units: "tb" });
// 1,00 TB
```

## units=""

```js
filterFileSize(1024, { units: "" });
// 1,00 KB

filterFileSize(1048576, { units: "" });
// 1,00 MB

filterFileSize(1073741824, { units: "" });
// 1,00 GB

filterFileSize(1073741824 * 1024, { units: "" });
// 1,00 TB
```

## sourceUnits

```js
filterFileSize(1024, { sourceUnits: "b" });
// 1,00 KB

filterFileSize(2, { sourceUnits: "kb" });
// 2,00 KB

filterFileSize(1, { sourceUnits: "mb" });
// 1.024,00 KB

filterFileSize(0.1, { sourceUnits: "gb" });
// 104.857,60 KB

filterFileSize(0.0001, { sourceUnits: "tb" });
// 107.374,18 KB
```

## digits

```js
filterFileSize(1024, { digits: 0 });
// 1 KB

filterFileSize(10241, { digits: 2 });
// 10,00 KB
```

## Translations

| key | en |
| --- | --- |
| `_A_FILE_SIZE_B_` | Bytes |
| `_A_FILE_SIZE_KB_` | KB |
| `_A_FILE_SIZE_MB_` | MB |
| `_A_FILE_SIZE_GB_` | GB |
| `_A_FILE_SIZE_TB_` | TB |
| `_A_FILE_SIZE_PB_` | PB |
| `_A_FILE_SIZE_EB_` | EB |
| `_A_FILE_SIZE_ZB_` | ZB |
| `_A_FILE_SIZE_YB_` | YB |

The function **filterFloat** formats numeric values according to the specified parameters. # filterInitials

The function **filterInitials** returns the initials of a name, e.g. for an avatar. If a name has more words than the limit, the initials of the first words and of the last word are used.

## Import as Function

```js
import { filterInitials } from "aloha-vue";
```

## Import as composition API

```js
import { AFiltersAPI } from "aloha-vue";

export default {
  setup() {  
    const {
      filterInitials,
    } = AFiltersAPI();
  },
};
```

## Arguments

```js
filterInitials(value, { [limit=2], [isUppercase=true] })
```

- **value** (String): The name
- **[limit=2]** (Number): The maximum number of initials
- **[isUppercase=true]** (Boolean): Whether the initials are converted to uppercase

## Basic usage

```js
filterInitials("Ilia Brykin");
// IB

filterInitials("Anna Maria Schmidt");
// AS

filterInitials("Anna-Lena Müller");
// AM

filterInitials("Ölçer Ünal");
// ÖÜ

filterInitials("Max");
// M
```

## limit

```js
filterInitials("Anna Maria Schmidt", { limit: 3 });
// AMS

filterInitials("Anna Maria Schmidt", { limit: 1 });
// A
```

## isUppercase

```js
filterInitials("anna schmidt", { isUppercase: false });
// as
```

## Avatar

Together with the class `a_rounded_circle`. The initials are hidden from screen readers with `aria-hidden`, because the name is shown next to them.

```html
<div
  v-for="user in users"
  :key="user.name"
  class="a_d_flex a_align_items_center a_gap_2"
>
  <span
    class="a_rounded_circle a_bg_primary a_color_white a_d_inline_flex a_align_items_center a_justify_content_center"
    style="width: 2.5rem; height: 2.5rem;"
    aria-hidden="true"
  >{{ user.initials }}</span>
  <span>{{ user.name }}</span>
</div>
```

```js
import {
  filterInitials,
} from "aloha-vue";

const users = [
  "Ilia Brykin",
  "Anna Maria Schmidt",
  "Ölçer Ünal",
].map(name => ({
  name,
  initials: filterInitials(name),
}));
```

# filterJson

The function **filterJson** converts a JavaScript object or value into a formatted JSON string. It allows customization of the **replacer** (function to alter the behavior of the conversion) and indentation (number of spaces or other characters for indentation).

## Import as Function

```js
import { filterJson } from "aloha-vue";
```

## Import as composition API

```js
import { AFiltersAPI } from "aloha-vue";

export default {
  setup() {  
    const {
      filterJson,
    } = AFiltersAPI();
  },
};
```

## Arguments

```js
filterJson(value, { [replacer], [space=2], [isHtml=false], [jsonClass="a_code_content"], [tag="pre"] })
```

- **value** (Any): The value or JavaScript object to be converted into a JSON string
- **[replacer]** (Function | Array): A function that affects the behavior of the conversion process, or an array of strings and numbers that specifies properties of value to be included in the output. If **replacer** is an array, all elements in this array that are not strings or numbers (neither primitive values nor wrapper objects), including symbol values, are completely ignored. If **replacer** is anything other than a function or an array (e.g., null or not specified), all string-based properties of the object are included in the resulting JSON string
- **[space=2]** (Number | String): A string or number used for inserting white space (including indentation, newline characters, etc.) into the output JSON string for readability purposes. If this is a number, it indicates the number of spaces or other characters to be used as indentation, limited to a maximum of 10 (i.e., any number greater than 10 is treated as though it were 10). Values less than 1 indicate that no white space should be used. If this is a string, the string (or the first 10 characters of the string if it's longer than that) is inserted before each nested object or array. If **space** is anything other than a string or number (can be either a primitive or a wrapper object) — e.g., null or not specified — no white space is used
- **[isHtml=false]** (Boolean): Determines if the output should be formatted as HTML. When set to false, the output is returned as a plain text string.
- **[jsonClass=a_code_content]** (String): The CSS class to be applied when `isHtml` is true.
- **[tag=pre]** (String): The HTML tag to wrap the formatted JSON string when `isHtml` is true.

## Basic usage

```js
filterJson({ x: 5, y: 6 });
// {
  "x": 5,
  "y": 6
}

filterJson({ x: "aloha", y: 6 });
// {
  "x": "aloha",
  "y": 6
}

filterJson(true);
// true

filterJson("aloha");
// "aloha"

filterJson([1, "false", false]);
// [
  1,
  "false",
  false
]

filterJson([NaN, null, Infinity, undefined]);
// [
  null,
  null,
  null,
  null
]
```

## space

```js
filterJson({ x: 5, y: 6 }, { space: 0 });
// {"x":5,"y":6}

filterJson({ x: 5, y: 6 }, { space: 1 });
// {
 "x": 5,
 "y": 6
}

filterJson({ x: 5, y: 6 }, { space: "\t" });
// {
	"x": 5,
	"y": 6
}
```

## replacer

```js
function replacer(key, value) {
  // Filtering out properties
  if (typeof value === "string") {
    return undefined;
  }
  return value;
}

const aloha = {
  foundation: "Mozilla",
  model: "box",
  week: 45,
  transport: "car",
  month: 7,
};

filterJson(aloha, { replacer });
// {
  "week": 45,
  "month": 7
}

filterJson(aloha, { replacer: ["week", "month", "model"] });
// {
  "week": 45,
  "month": 7,
  "model": "box"
}
```

## isHtml

```js
filterJson({ x: 5, y: 6 }, { isHtml: true });
// <pre class="a_code_content">{
  "x": 5,
  "y": 6
}</pre>

filterJson({ x: 5, y: 6 }, { isHtml: false });
// {
  "x": 5,
  "y": 6
}
```

## jsonClass

```js
filterJson({ x: 5, y: 6 }, { isHtml: true, class: "aloha" });
// <pre class="a_code_content">{
  "x": 5,
  "y": 6
}</pre>
```

## tag

```js
filterJson({ x: 5, y: 6 }, { isHtml: true, tag: "pre" });
// <pre class="a_code_content">{
  "x": 5,
  "y": 6
}</pre>

filterJson({ x: 5, y: 6 }, { isHtml: true, tag: "div" });
// <div class="a_code_content">{
  "x": 5,
  "y": 6
}</div>
```

# filterLink

The function **filterLink** creates an HTML link based on the provided URL. It allows customization of the protocol, target, CSS class, and displayed text for the link. The function checks the validity of the URL and ensures that it is safely inserted into the HTML link.

## Import as Function

```js
import { filterLink } from "aloha-vue";
```

## Import as composition API

```js
import { AFiltersAPI } from "aloha-vue";

export default {
  setup() {  
    const {
      filterLink,
    } = AFiltersAPI();
  },
};
```

## Arguments

```js
filterLink(url, { [linkText=""], [protocol="https://"], [target=""], [linkClass=""] })
```

- **url** (String): The URL to be inserted into the HTML link
- **[linkText=""]** (String): The text that will be displayed in the HTML link. If not specified, the URL is used
- **[protocol="https://"]** (String): The protocol to be added before the URL
- **[target=""]** (String): The **target** attribute for the HTML link, which controls the behavior when opening the link
- **[linkClass=""]** (String): A CSS class that will be added to the HTML link

## Basic usage

```js
filterLink("example.com");
// <a href="https://example.com">example.com</a>

filterLink("https://example.com");
// <a href="https://example.com">https://example.com</a>
```

## linkText

```js
filterLink("example.com", { linkText: "example" });
// <a href="https://example.com">example</a>

filterLink("https://example.com", { linkText: "Aloha" });
// <a href="https://example.com">Aloha</a>
```

## protocol

```js
filterLink("example.com", { protocol: "" });
// <a href="example.com">example.com</a>

filterLink("https://example.com", { protocol: "http://" });
// <a href="http://example.com">example.com</a>
```

## target

```js
filterLink("example.com", { target: "_blank" });
// <a href="https://example.com" target="_blank">example.com</a>

filterLink("https://example.com", { target: "_self" });
// <a href="https://example.com" target="_self">example.com</a>

filterLink("https://example.com", { target: "_parent" });
// <a href="https://example.com" target="_parent">example.com</a>

filterLink("https://example.com", { target: "_top" });
// <a href="https://example.com" target="_top">example.com</a>
```

## linkClass

```js
filterLink("example.com", { linkClass: "a_btn a_btn_link" });
// <a href="https://example.com" class="a_btn a_btn_link">example.com</a>
```

# filterList

The function creates a list from an array.

## Import as Function

```js
import { filterList } from "aloha-vue";
```

## Import as composition API

```js
import { AFiltersAPI } from "aloha-vue";

export default {
  setup() {  
    const {
      filterList,
    } = AFiltersAPI();
  },
};
```

## Arguments

```js
filterList(array, { [defaultValue=""], [isHtml=true], [isSimpleArray=false], [keyChildren=""], [keyLabel=""], [keyLabelCallback], [lastSeparator], [listClass=""], [separator], [separatorHtml=", "], [tag="ul"] })
```

- **array** (Array): The array for the list
- **[defaultValue=""]** (String): Value returned if the array is empty or not an array
- **[isHtml=true]** (Boolean): If **True**, an HTML list (<ul><li>...</li></ul>) is created. Otherwise, a text list is generated
- **[isSimpleArray=false]** (Boolean): Indicates whether only a simple array without objects is used
- **[keyChildren=""]** (String): Key for child elements (only if **isSimpleArray=false**)
- **[keyLabel=""]** (String): Key for the label to be displayed (only if **isSimpleArray=false**)
- **[keyLabelCallback]** (Function): Function for generating labels with two parameters (**item**, **itemIndex**)
- **[lastSeparator]** (String): Specifies the separator to be used before the final element in the list.
- **[listClass=""]** (String): CSS class e.g.: (a_list_without_styles)
- **[separator]** (String): Separator between elements (only if **isHtml=false**)
- **[separatorHtml=""]** (String): HTML between the elements, e.g. a line break (only if **isHtml=true**)
- **[tag="ul"]** (String): HTML tag for the entire list

## isSimpleArray=true

```js
const ITEMS = ["label 1", "label 2", "label 3"];

filterList(ITEMS, {
  isSimpleArray: true,
});
// <ul><li>label 1</li><li>label 2</li><li>label 3</li></ul>
```

## keyLabel

```js
const ITEMS = [
  {
    label: "label 1",
  },
  {
    label: "label 2",
  },
  {
    label: "label 3",
  },
  {
    label: "label 4",
  },
];

filterList(ITEMS, {
  keyLabel: "label",
});
// <ul><li>label 1</li><li>label 2</li><li>label 3</li><li>label 4</li></ul>
```

## keyLabelCallback

```js
const ITEMS = [
  {
    label: "label 1",
  },
  {
    label: "label 2",
  },
  {
    label: "label 3",
  },
  {
    label: "label 4",
  },
];

const keyLabelCallback = ({ item }) => {
  return `+ ${ item.label }`;
};

filterList(ITEMS, {
  keyLabelCallback,
});
// <ul><li>+ label 1</li><li>+ label 2</li><li>+ label 3</li><li>+ label 4</li></ul>
```

## isHtml=false

```js
const ITEMS = ["label 1", "label 2", "label 3"];

filterList(ITEMS, {
  isHtml: false,
  isSimpleArray: true,
});
// label 1, label 2, label 3
```

## separator / lastSeparator

```js
const ITEMS = ["label 1", "label 2", "label 3"];

filterList(ITEMS, {
  isHtml: false,
  isSimpleArray: true,
  separator: "; ",
});
// label 1; label 2; label 3

filterList(ITEMS, {
  isHtml: false,
  isSimpleArray: true,
  lastSeparator: " & ",
  separator: ", ",
});
// label 1, label 2 & label 3

filterList(ITEMS, {
  isHtml: true,
  isSimpleArray: true,
  separator: ";",
});
// <ul><li>label 1;</li><li>label 2;</li><li>label 3</li></ul>
```

## separatorHtml

```js
const ITEMS = ["label 1", "label 2", "label 3"];

filterList(ITEMS, {
  isHtml: true,
  isSimpleArray: true,
  separatorHtml: "<hr>",
});
// <ul><li>label 1<hr></li><li>label 2<hr></li><li>label 3</li></ul>

filterList(ITEMS, {
  isHtml: true,
  isSimpleArray: true,
  separatorHtml: "<div>Aloha</div>",
});
// <ul><li>label 1<div>Aloha</div></li><li>label 2<div>Aloha</div></li><li>label 3</li></ul>
```

## tag

```js
const ITEMS = ["label 1", "label 2", "label 3"];

filterList(ITEMS, {
  tag: "ol",
  isSimpleArray: true,
});
// <ol><li>label 1</li><li>label 2</li><li>label 3</li></ol>
```

## listClass

```js
const ITEMS = ["label 1", "label 2", "label 3"];

filterList(ITEMS, {
  listClass: "a_list_without_styles",
  isSimpleArray: true,
});
// <ul class="a_list_without_styles"><li>label 1</li><li>label 2</li><li>label 3</li></ul>
```

## keyChildren

```js
const ITEMS = [
  {
    label: "Level 1",
    children: [
      {
        label: "Level 1.1",
        children: [
          {
            label: "Level 1.1.1",
          },
          {
            label: "Level 1.1.2",
          },
        ],
      },
      {
        label: "Level 1.2",
      },
    ],
  },
  {
    label: "Level 2",
    children: [
      {
        label: "Level 2.1",
      },
      {
        label: "Level 2.2",
      },
    ],
  },
];

filterList(ITEMS, {
  keyLabel: "label",
  keyChildren: "children",
});
// <ul><li>Level 1<ul><li>Level 1.1<ul><li>Level 1.1.1</li><li>Level 1.1.2</li></ul></li><li>Level 1.2</li></ul></li><li>Level 2<ul><li>Level 2.1</li><li>Level 2.2</li></ul></li></ul>
```

## Tree structure isSimpleArray=true

```js
const ITEMS = [
  "Level 1",
    [
      "Level 2",
      [
        "Level 2.1",
        "Level 2.2",
      ],
    ],
    [
      "Level 3",
      [
        "Level 3.1",
        [
          "Level 3.2",
          [
            "Level 3.2.1",
            "Level 3.2.2",
          ],
        ],
      ],
    ],
  ];

filterList(ITEMS, {
  isSimpleArray: true,
});
// <ul><li>Level 1</li><li>Level 2<ul><li>Level 2.1</li><li>Level 2.2</li></ul></li><li>Level 3<ul><li>Level 3.1</li><li>Level 3.2<ul><li>Level 3.2.1</li><li>Level 3.2.2</li></ul></li></ul></li></ul>

filterList([["x1", ["x1.1", "x1.2"]], { isSimpleArray: true })
// <ul><li>x1<ul><li>x1.1</li><li>x1.2</li></ul></li></ul>

filterList(["x0", ["x1", ["x1.1", "x1.2"]], "x3"], { isSimpleArray: true })
// <ul><li>x0</li><li>x1<ul><li>x1.1</li><li>x1.2</li></ul></li><li>x3</li></ul>
```

# filterMask

# filterNumberCompact

The function **filterNumberCompact** shortens a large number with a unit (thousand, million, billion, trillion), e.g. for counters, badges and dashboards. The number is formatted like **filterFloat**.

## Import as Function

```js
import { filterNumberCompact } from "aloha-vue";
```

## Import as composition API

```js
import { AFiltersAPI } from "aloha-vue";

export default {
  setup() {  
    const {
      filterNumberCompact,
    } = AFiltersAPI();
  },
};
```

## Arguments

```js
filterNumberCompact(value, { [digits=1], [minValue=1000], [isTrailingZeros=false] })
```

- **value** (Number | String): The number
- **[digits=1]** (Number): The number of decimal places of a shortened number
- **[minValue=1000]** (Number): Numbers below this value (by amount) are not shortened
- **[isTrailingZeros=false]** (Boolean): Whether **1,0** is shown instead of **1**

## Basic usage

```js
filterNumberCompact(1234567);
// 1,2 M

filterNumberCompact(15300);
// 15,3 K

filterNumberCompact(2500000000);
// 2,5 B

filterNumberCompact(999);
// 999
```

## digits

```js
filterNumberCompact(1234567, { digits: 2 });
// 1,23 M

filterNumberCompact(1234567, { digits: 0 });
// 1 M
```

## minValue

```js
filterNumberCompact(15300, { minValue: 100000 });
// 15.300

filterNumberCompact(153000, { minValue: 100000 });
// 153 K
```

## isTrailingZeros

```js
filterNumberCompact(1000000);
// 1 M

filterNumberCompact(1000000, { isTrailingZeros: true });
// 1,0 M
```

## Translations

| key | en |
| --- | --- |
| `_A_NUMBER_COMPACT_THOUSAND_` | K |
| `_A_NUMBER_COMPACT_MILLION_` | M |
| `_A_NUMBER_COMPACT_BILLION_` | B |
| `_A_NUMBER_COMPACT_TRILLION_` | T |

# filterPercent

The function **filterPercent** formats a value as a percentage, e.g. "15,30 %". It uses **filterFloat**.

## Import as Function

```js
import { filterPercent } from "aloha-vue";
```

## Import as composition API

```js
import { AFiltersAPI } from "aloha-vue";

export default {
  setup() {  
    const {
      filterPercent,
    } = AFiltersAPI();
  },
};
```

## Arguments

```js
filterPercent(value, { [digits=2], [digitGrouping=true], [isFraction=false] })
```

- **value** (Number | String): The value to format
- **[digits=2]** (Number): The number of decimal places
- **[digitGrouping=true]** (Boolean): Whether digit grouping separators are shown
- **[isFraction=false]** (Boolean): Whether the value is a fraction (0.153 → 15,30 %) and not a percentage (15.3 → 15,30 %)

## Basic usage

```js
filterPercent(15.3);
// 15,30 %

filterPercent("99,5");
// 99,50 %

filterPercent(12345.678);
// 12.345,68 %
```

```js
filterPercent(15.36, { digits: 1 });
// 15,4 %

filterPercent(12345, { digits: 0, digitGrouping: false });
// 12345 %
```

## isFraction

```js
filterPercent(0.153, { isFraction: true });
// 15,30 %

filterPercent(1, { isFraction: true, digits: 0 });
// 100 %
```

# filterPropertyByValue

The function **filterPropertyByValue** allows for mapping values to predefined properties in a mapping object. It checks if the passed value exists as a key in the mapping object. If so, the associated property is returned; otherwise, the default value is used.

## Import as Function

```js
import { filterPropertyByValue } from "aloha-vue";
```

## Import as composition API

```js
import { AFiltersAPI } from "aloha-vue";

export default {
  setup() {  
    const {
      filterPropertyByValue,
    } = AFiltersAPI();
  },
};
```

## Arguments

```js
filterPropertyByValue(value, { [mapping={}], [defaultValue=""] })
```

- **value** (Any): The value that should be mapped to a property in the mapping object
- **[mapping={}]** (Object): An object that defines the mapping of values to properties
- **[defaultValue=""]** (String): The default value returned if the passed value is not found in the mapping object

## mapping

```js
filterPropertyByValue("111", { mapping: { aloha: "1", holla: "2" } });
// 
filterPropertyByValue("aloha", { mapping: { aloha: "1", holla: "2" } });
// 1
```

## defaultValue

```js
filterPropertyByValue("111", { mapping: { aloha: "1", holla: "2" }, defaultValue: "not found" });
// not found
filterPropertyByValue("222", { mapping: { aloha: "1", holla: "2" }, defaultValue: "0" });
// 0
```

<!-- https://ilia-brykin.github.io/aloha/llms/functions/filter-search-highlight.md -->

# filterSearchHighlight

The function **filterSearchHighlight** is used to mark a search term in a value by enclosing the search term with **HTML** tags. It allows customization of the search term and the **CSS** class for highlighting.

## Import as Function

```js
import { filterSearchHighlight } from "aloha-vue";
```

## Import as composition API

```js
import { AFiltersAPI } from "aloha-vue";

export default {
  setup() {  
    const {
      filterSearchHighlight,
    } = AFiltersAPI();
  },
};
```

## Arguments

```js
filterSearchHighlight(value, { [searchModel=""], [searchClass="a_search_highlight"], [tag="mark"], [attributes=[]], [caseSensitive=false], [isHtml=false] })
```

- **value** (String): The value in which the search term should be highlighted
- **[searchModel=""]** (String): The search term that should be highlighted in the value
- **[searchClass="a_search_highlight"]** (String): A **CSS** class that should style the highlighted part of the value
- **[tag="mark"]** (String): The **HTML** tag to use instead of mark
- **[attributes=[]]** (String): List of additional attributes in the format **['key="value"', 'key2="value2"']**
- **[caseSensitive=false]** (Boolean): Whether the search should be case-sensitive
- **[isHtml=false]** (Boolean): Whether to interpret value as **HTML** and search inside text content only.

## searchModel

```js
filterSearchHighlight("Lorem ipsum dolor sit amet consectetur adipisicing elit.", { searchModel: "ipsum" });
// Lorem <mark class="a_search_highlight">ipsum</mark> dolor sit amet consectetur adipisicing elit.

filterSearchHighlight("Lorem ipsum dolor sit amet consectetur adipisicing elit.", { searchModel: "it" });
// Lorem ipsum dolor s<mark class="a_search_highlight">it</mark> amet consectetur adipisicing el<mark class="a_search_highlight">it</mark>.

filterSearchHighlight("Lorem ipsum dolor sit amet consectetur adipisicing elit.", { searchModel: "aloha" });
// Lorem ipsum dolor sit amet consectetur adipisicing elit.
```

## searchClass

```js
filterSearchHighlight("Lorem ipsum dolor sit amet consectetur adipisicing elit.", { searchModel: "ipsum", searchClass: "test_class" });
// Lorem <mark class="test_class">ipsum</mark> dolor sit amet consectetur adipisicing elit.
```

## tag

```js
filterSearchHighlight("Lorem ipsum dolor sit amet consectetur adipisicing elit.", { searchModel: "ipsum", tag: "strong" });
// Lorem <strong class="a_search_highlight">ipsum</strong> dolor sit amet consectetur adipisicing elit.
```

## attributes

```js
filterSearchHighlight("Lorem ipsum dolor sit amet consectetur adipisicing elit.", { searchModel: "ipsum", attributes: ["data-aloha='search'", "title='Highlight'"] });
// Lorem <mark class="a_search_highlight" data-aloha='search' title='Highlight'>ipsum</mark> dolor sit amet consectetur adipisicing elit.
```

## caseSensitive

```js
filterSearchHighlight("Aloha Vue vue.", { searchModel: "Vue", caseSensitive: true });
// Aloha <mark class="a_search_highlight">Vue</mark> vue.

filterSearchHighlight("Aloha Vue vue.", { searchModel: "Vue", caseSensitive: false });
// Aloha <mark class="a_search_highlight">Vue</mark> <mark class="a_search_highlight">vue</mark>.
```

## isHtml

```js
filterSearchHighlight("Aloha <strong>Vue</strong> is a <a href="https://vue.com">framework</a>", { searchModel: "vue", isHtml: true });
// Aloha <strong><mark class="a_search_highlight">Vue</mark></strong> is a <a href="https://vue.com">framework</a>

filterSearchHighlight("<div><p>Vue is amazing.</p><span>Vue framework</span></div>", { searchModel: "vue", isHtml: true });
// <div><p><mark class="a_search_highlight">Vue</mark> is amazing.</p><span><mark class="a_search_highlight">Vue</mark> framework</span></div>

filterSearchHighlight("<div><h1>Vue.js</h1><p>This is a Vue framework.</p></div>", { searchModel: "vue", isHtml: true });
// <div><h1><mark class="a_search_highlight">Vue</mark>.js</h1><p>This is a <mark class="a_search_highlight">Vue</mark> framework.</p></div>

filterSearchHighlight("<p>Welcome to <strong>Vue</strong><span>.js</span> world.</p>", { searchModel: "vue", isHtml: true });
// <p>Welcome to <strong><mark class="a_search_highlight">Vue</mark></strong><span>.js</span> world.</p>
```

# filterTruncateMiddle

The function **filterTruncateMiddle** shortens a string in the middle and keeps its start and its end, e.g. for IDs, hashes, IBANs or file paths. Use **filterLimitTo** to shorten a text at the end.

## Import as Function

```js
import { filterTruncateMiddle } from "aloha-vue";
```

## Import as composition API

```js
import { AFiltersAPI } from "aloha-vue";

export default {
  setup() {  
    const {
      filterTruncateMiddle,
    } = AFiltersAPI();
  },
};
```

## Arguments

```js
filterTruncateMiddle(value, { [start=6], [end=4], [separator="…"] })
```

- **value** (String | Number): The value to shorten
- **[start=6]** (Number): The number of characters kept at the start
- **[end=4]** (Number): The number of characters kept at the end
- **[separator="…"]** (String): The text put in place of the removed characters

## Basic usage

```js
filterTruncateMiddle("3f9a1c7e-42b0-4d1e-9c55-7a1d2e3f4b5c");
// 3f9a1c…4b5c

filterTruncateMiddle("Short");
// Short
```

## start, end

```js
filterTruncateMiddle("DE89370400440532013000", { start: 4, end: 4 });
// DE89…3000

filterTruncateMiddle("3f9a1c7e-42b0-4d1e-9c55", { start: 8, end: 0 });
// 3f9a1c7e…
```

## separator

```js
filterTruncateMiddle("/home/user/projects/aloha/src/index.js", { start: 5, end: 8, separator: "/…/" });
// /home/…/index.js

filterTruncateMiddle("0x71C7656EC7ab88b098defB751B7401B5f6d8976F", { separator: "..." });
// 0x71C7...976F
```

# filterValueByCondition

The function **filterValueByCondition** returns a result based on the first matching condition. Conditions can be functions or JavaScript expression strings. Results can be static values, functions, or template strings.

String expressions and templates are executed as JavaScript. Use them only with trusted configuration and never with unchecked user input.

## Import as Function

```js
import { filterValueByCondition } from "aloha-vue";
```

## Import as composition API

```js
import { AFiltersAPI } from "aloha-vue";

export default {
  setup() {  
    const {
      filterValueByCondition,
    } = AFiltersAPI();
  },
};
```

## Arguments

```js
filterValueByCondition(value, { [conditions=[]], [defaultValue=""], [defaultTemplate] })
```

- **value** (Any): The value that is checked by conditions and can be used in functions, expressions, and templates.
- **[conditions=[]]** (Array): An ordered list of condition objects. The first matching condition defines the returned value.
- **[conditions[].if]** (Function | String): A function or JavaScript expression string that receives the current value and decides whether the condition matches.
- **[conditions[].then]** (Any | Function): A static value or function returned when the condition matches.
- **[conditions[].thenTemplate]** (String): A JavaScript template string used when the condition matches. The current value is available as value.
- **[defaultValue=""]** (Any | Function): A static value or function returned when no condition matches.
- **[defaultTemplate]** (String): A JavaScript template string returned when no condition matches. The current value is available as value.

## Function conditions

```js
const options = {
  conditions: [
    {
      if: value => value > 3,
      then: value => `(${ value * 3 } Aloha)`,
    },
    {
      if: value => value < 2,
      then: "aloha",
    },
  ],
  defaultValue: value => value / 2,
};

filterValueByCondition(4, options);
// (12 Aloha)
filterValueByCondition(1, options);
// aloha
filterValueByCondition(2, options);
// 1
```

## String expressions and templates

```js
const options = {
  conditions: [
    {
      if: "value > 3",
      thenTemplate: "(${ value * 3 } Aloha)",
    },
    {
      if: "value < 2",
      then: "aloha",
    },
  ],
  defaultTemplate: "${ value / 2 }",
};

filterValueByCondition(4, options);
// (12 Aloha)
filterValueByCondition(1, options);
// aloha
filterValueByCondition(2, options);
// 1
```

## Mixed conditions

```js
const options = {
  conditions: [
    {
      if: value => value === 0,
      then: "zero",
    },
    {
      if: "value > 3",
      thenTemplate: "(${ value * 3 } Aloha)",
    },
    {
      if: value => value < 2,
      then: value => `small: ${ value }`,
    },
  ],
  defaultTemplate: "${ value / 2 }",
};

filterValueByCondition(0, options);
// zero
filterValueByCondition(4, options);
// (12 Aloha)
filterValueByCondition(1, options);
// small: 1
filterValueByCondition(2, options);
// 1
```

<!-- https://ilia-brykin.github.io/aloha/llms/functions/utils-aorder-by.md -->

# aOrderBy

Extends lodash's orderBy with case-insensitive comparison by default while preserving all iteratee and order combinations.

## Import as Function

```js
import { aOrderBy } from "aloha-vue";
```

## Arguments

```js
aOrderBy(collection, iteratees?, orders?, options?)
```

- **collection** (Array | Object): Collection to iterate over (array or object).
- **iteratees** (String | Function | Array | Object | Null): Iteratees that define the sort criteria; accepts property paths, functions, arrays, shorthand objects, or null.
- **orders** (String | Array | Null): Sort directions that correspond to iteratees (e.g., "asc", "desc"); accepts string, array, or null.
- **options** (Object): Optional configuration object ({ caseSensitive?: boolean }) passed as the last argument.

## Basic usage

```js
const users = [
  { name: "beta" },
  { name: "Alpha" },
  { name: "gamma" },
  { name: "delta" },
  { name: "alpha" },
];

aOrderBy(users, "name").map(user => user.name);
// ["Alpha","alpha","beta","delta","gamma"]

aOrderBy(users, "name", "desc").map(user => user.name);
// ["gamma","delta","beta","Alpha","alpha"]

const scoredUsers = [
  { name: "alex", score: 5 },
  { name: "Alex", score: 3 },
  { name: "alex", score: 2 },
  { name: "alex", score: 7 },
];

aOrderBy(scoredUsers, ["name", user => user.score], ["asc", "asc"])
  .map(user => user.name + ":" + user.score);
// ["alex:2","Alex:3","alex:5","alex:7"]

const employees = [
  { profile: { lastName: "Davis" }, age: 40 },
  { profile: { lastName: "davis" }, age: 25 },
  { profile: { lastName: "Anders" }, age: 32 },
  { profile: { lastName: "anders" }, age: 29 },
];

aOrderBy(employees, ["profile.lastName", user => user.age], ["asc", "desc"])
  .map(employee => employee.profile.lastName + ":" + employee.age);
// ["Anders:32","anders:29","Davis:40","davis:25"]

const codes = [
  { code: "abC" },
  { code: "abc" },
  { code: "Abd" },
];

aOrderBy(codes, "code").map(item => item.code);
// ["abC","abc","Abd"]

aOrderBy(codes, "code", "asc", { caseSensitive: true }).map(item => item.code);
// ["Abd","abC","abc"]
```

<!-- https://ilia-brykin.github.io/aloha/llms/functions/utils-asort-by.md -->

# aSortBy

Extends lodash's sortBy with case-insensitive comparison by default while keeping support for every iteratee shorthand.

## Import as Function

```js
import { aSortBy } from "aloha-vue";
```

## Arguments

```js
aSortBy(collection, ...iteratees, options?)
```

- **collection** (Array | Object): Collection to iterate over (array or object).
- **...iteratees** (String | Function | Array | Object): Iteratees that describe the sort criteria; accepts property paths, functions, arrays, or shorthand objects.
- **options** (Object): Optional configuration object ({ caseSensitive?: boolean }) passed as the last argument.

## Basic usage

```js
const users = [
  { name: "beta" },
  { name: "Alpha" },
  { name: "gamma" },
];

aSortBy(users, "name").map(user => user.name);
// ["Alpha","beta","gamma"]

const scoredUsers = [
  { name: "alex", score: 5 },
  { name: "Alex", score: 3 },
  { name: "alex", score: 2 },
  { name: "alex", score: 7 },
];

aSortBy(scoredUsers, ["name", user => user.score]).map(user => user.name + ":" + user.score);
// ["alex:2","Alex:3","alex:5","alex:7"]

const mixedUsers = [
  { profile: { lastName: "Davis" }, status: "active" },
  { profile: { lastName: "anders" }, status: "inactive" },
  { profile: { lastName: "Anders" }, status: "active" },
];

aSortBy(mixedUsers, ["profile.lastName", { status: "active" }]).map(user => user.profile.lastName + ":" + user.status);
// ["anders:inactive","Anders:active","Davis:active"]

const codes = [
  { code: "abC" },
  { code: "abc" },
  { code: "Abd" },
];

aSortBy(codes, "code").map(item => item.code);
// ["abC","abc","Abd"]

aSortBy(codes, "code", { caseSensitive: true }).map(item => item.code);
// ["Abd","abC","abc"]
```

# getTotalNestedCount

Calculates the total count of elements within a nested structure, including all children and sub-children, based on the specified child key.

## Import as Function

```js
import { getTotalNestedCount } from "aloha-vue";
```

## Arguments

```js
getTotalNestedCount({ array, keyChildren })
```

- **array** (Array): The initial array to traverse for counting
- **keyChildren** (String): The key used to identify child elements within each object in the array

## Basic usage

```js
getTotalNestedCount({ array: ["hello", "Aloha"], keyChildren: "" });
// 2

getTotalNestedCount({ array: [], keyChildren: "" });
// 0

getTotalNestedCount({ array: [{ children: ["hello", "world"] }, "test"], keyChildren: "children" });
// 4

getTotalNestedCount({ array: [{ aloha: [{ aloha: ["hello", "world"] }, { aloha: ["hello1", "world1"] }] }, "test"], keyChildren: "aloha" });
// 8
```


```js

```

- **value** (Number): The number to check if it is even

```js
// true

// true

// true

isEven(-2);
// true

isEven(1);
// false
isEven(3);
// false
isEven(353);
// false

isEven(-1);
// false

isEven(2.5);
// false

isEven("Aloha");
// false
isEven(null);
// false
isEven(undefined);
// false
```
